original: Given `@/replay` is imported, when the module exports are inspected, then it exposes `inferPhases` as a callable function.
refined: After `import { inferPhases } from '@/replay'`, `typeof inferPhases === 'function'` is true and `inferPhases.length === 2` (arity: entries, storyId).

original: [inferPhases] returns a phase list containing an entry with `name === "implementer"` and `status === "pass"` when given a log-entry array containing `{ stage: "story-orchestrator", message: "Phase passed: implementer", data: { storyId: "US-002" } }` and called as `inferPhases(entries, "US-002")`.
refined: Given `entries = [{ stage: 'story-orchestrator', message: 'Phase passed: implementer', data: { storyId: 'US-002' } }]`, calling `inferPhases(entries, 'US-002')` returns an array where `result[0].name === 'implementer' && result[0].status === 'pass' && result.length === 1`.

original: [inferPhases] returns phase names exactly `["test-writer", "implementer"]` in that order when given `Phase passed: test-writer` followed by `Phase passed: implementer` for `storyId "US-002"`.
refined: Given `entries` containing two entries in order: `{ stage: 'story-orchestrator', message: 'Phase passed: test-writer', data: { storyId: 'US-002' } }` then `{ stage: 'story-orchestrator', message: 'Phase passed: implementer', data: { storyId: 'US-002' } }`, calling `inferPhases(entries, 'US-002')` returns an array where `result.map(p => p.name)` equals exactly `['test-writer', 'implementer']` and `result.length === 2`.

original: [inferPhases] returns a phase list containing an entry with `name === "full-suite-gate"` and `status === "fail"` when given `{ stage: "story-orchestrator", message: "Phase failed: full-suite-gate", data: { storyId: "US-002" } }`.
refined: Given `entries = [{ stage: 'story-orchestrator', message: 'Phase failed: full-suite-gate', data: { storyId: 'US-002' } }]`, calling `inferPhases(entries, 'US-002')` returns an array where `result.some(p => p.name === 'full-suite-gate' && p.status === 'fail')` is true.

original: [inferPhases] returns a non-empty escalation list for `US-002` when given an entry `{ stage: "agent-manager", message: "fail-stale: immediate same-agent retry", data: { storyId: "US-002" } }`.
refined: Given `entries = [{ stage: 'agent-manager', message: 'fail-stale: immediate same-agent retry', data: { storyId: 'US-002' } }]`, calling `inferPhases(entries, 'US-002')` returns an object where `result.escalations !== undefined && Array.isArray(result.escalations) && result.escalations.length > 0` is true.

original: Given `@/replay` is imported, when the module exports are inspected, then it exposes `reconstructTimeline`.
refined: After `import { reconstructTimeline } from '@/replay'`, `typeof reconstructTimeline === 'function'` is true and `reconstructTimeline.length >= 2` (arity: logSpine, metrics, optional registry).

original: [reconstructTimeline] returns a `RunTimeline` whose `runId` and `feature` equal the metrics and registry values and whose `stories` length equals the number of stories in the matching `RunMetrics` entry when given a parsed log spine plus a matching `RunMetrics` entry.
refined: Given `logSpine` with run-start event, `runMetrics` with 3 stories, and `registry` with matching runId, calling `reconstructTimeline(logSpine, runMetrics, registry)` returns an object where `result.runId === runMetrics.runId && result.feature === registry.feature && result.stories.length === runMetrics.stories.length`.

original: [reconstructTimeline] returns a `StoryTimeline` with `status === "passed"`, `finalTier === "balanced"`, `cost === 0.42`, and `attempts === 2` when the matching `StoryMetrics` entry has `success: true, finalTier: "balanced", cost: 0.42, attempts: 2`.
refined: Given `storyMetrics = { storyId: 'US-002', success: true, finalTier: 'balanced', cost: 0.42, attempts: 2 }` and corresponding log spine, calling `reconstructTimeline(logSpine, runMetrics, registry)` returns a `StoryTimeline` in `result.stories` where `story.status === 'passed' && story.finalTier === 'balanced' && story.cost === 0.42 && story.attempts === 2`.

original: [reconstructTimeline] returns a `RunTimeline` with `status === "crashed"` and `StoryTimeline.cost === undefined` for each story when given a log spine and a `status.json` object carrying a crash signal but no matching `RunMetrics` entry.
refined: Given `logSpine` with crash signal and `status.json = { crashed: true, exitCode: 1 }` with no matching `RunMetrics`, calling `reconstructTimeline(logSpine, null, registry)` or equivalent degraded path returns `result.status === 'crashed' && result.stories.every(s => s.cost === undefined)`.

original: [reconstructTimeline] returns `rootCausePhaseIndex` equal to the index of the inferred failed phase when a story has `success: false` and its inferred phases end in a phase with `status === "fail"`.
refined: Given a story with `success: false` and inferred phases `['test-writer', 'implementer', 'full-suite-gate']` where `full-suite-gate.status === 'fail'` (last), calling `reconstructTimeline` returns a `StoryTimeline` where `story.rootCausePhaseIndex === 2` (0-indexed position of failed phase).

original: [reconstructTimeline] returns `inferred === true` on the `RunTimeline`.
refined: Calling `reconstructTimeline(logSpine, runMetrics, registry)` returns an object where `result.inferred === true`.

original: [reconstructTimeline] returns `naxVersion === "0.71.1"` when the log spine includes `{ stage: "run.start", data: { naxVersion: "0.71.1" } }`.
refined: Given `logSpine` containing `{ stage: 'run.start', data: { naxVersion: '0.71.1' } }`, calling `reconstructTimeline(logSpine, runMetrics, registry)` returns `result.naxVersion === '0.71.1'`.

original: Given `@/replay` is imported, when the module exports are inspected, then it exposes `discoverRun`.
refined: After importing from `@/replay`, `typeof discoverRun === 'function'` evaluates to true.

original: [discoverRun] resolves to an object whose `meta.feature` equals the registry meta feature and whose `jsonlPath` ends in `.jsonl` when given an injected runs-dir containing a `<dir>/meta.json` whose `runId` equals the query and called as `discoverRun("run-2026-07-04T10-51-37-987Z")`.
refined: When `discoverRun("run-2026-07-04T10-51-37-987Z")` is called with an injected mock whose registry contains a run with `runId: "run-2026-07-04T10-51-37-987Z"` and `meta.feature: "my-feature"`, the returned object satisfies `result.meta.feature === "my-feature"` and `result.jsonlPath.endsWith(".jsonl")` is true.

original: [discoverRun] resolves to that same run when called as `discoverRun("run-2026-07-04")` and the registry entry's `meta.runId` starts with the query.
refined: When `discoverRun("run-2026-07-04")` is called and the registry contains a run with `runId: "run-2026-07-04T10-51-37-987Z"`, the returned object's `meta.runId` is `"run-2026-07-04T10-51-37-987Z"`.

original: [discoverRun] resolves to the registry entry whose `runId` is lexicographically greatest when called with no argument and given two registry entries.
refined: When `discoverRun()` is called with no argument and the registry contains entries with `runId` values `["run-2026-07-04T10-51-37-987Z", "run-2026-08-04T10-51-37-987Z"]`, the returned object's `meta.runId` equals `"run-2026-08-04T10-51-37-987Z"`.

original: [discoverRun] throws a `NaxError` with `code === "RUN_NOT_FOUND"` when no registry entry matches the query.
refined: When `discoverRun("nonexistent-run")` is called and no registry entry matches, a `NaxError` is thrown with `error.code === "RUN_NOT_FOUND"`.

original: [discoverRun] throws a `NaxError` with `code === "RUN_NOT_FOUND"` when more than one registry entry matches the supplied run-id prefix.
refined: When `discoverRun("run-2026-07")` is called and the registry contains multiple entries with `runId` values that start with "run-2026-07" (e.g., "run-2026-07-04T10-51-37-987Z" and "run-2026-07-05T10-51-37-987Z"), a `NaxError` is thrown with `error.code === "RUN_NOT_FOUND"`.

original: Given `@/replay` is imported, when the module exports are inspected, then it exposes `renderReport`.
refined: Import `* as replay from '@/replay'` and assert `typeof replay.renderReport === 'function'`.

original: [renderReport] returns a string containing the passed story's id on a single summary line and the failed story's inferred phase names on their own lines when given a `RunTimeline` with one `passed` and one `failed` story and default options.
refined: Call `renderReport(timeline)` where timeline contains a passed story (id: "PASS-1", phases: [{name: "p1", status: "passed"}]) and a failed story (id: "FAIL-1", phases: [{name: "phase1", status: "fail"}, {name: "phase2", status: "fail"}]). Assert returned string: includes "PASS-1" exactly once, includes "FAIL-1" exactly once, includes "phase1" on its own line, includes "phase2" on its own line.

original: Given default options, [renderReport] returns no per-phase lines for a `passed` story and includes the failed story's phases.
refined: Call `renderReport(timeline)` with timeline containing passed story (id: "PASS-1", phases: [{name: "setup", status: "passed"}, {name: "execute", status: "passed"}]) and failed story (id: "FAIL-1", phases: [{name: "setup", status: "fail"}]). Assert returned string: contains no line matching `/^(?!.*PASS-1).*setup.*execute/` (no phase lines for PASS-1), and contains "setup" associated with FAIL-1.

original: [renderReport] returns a string containing a passed story's phase names when called with `{ all: true }`.
refined: Call `renderReport(timeline, { all: true })` where timeline contains passed story (id: "PASS-1", phases: [{name: "phaseA", status: "passed"}, {name: "phaseB", status: "passed"}]). Assert returned string contains "phaseA" and contains "phaseB".

original: [renderReport] returns a string containing US-002's block and not containing any other story id when called with `{ story: "US-002" }`.
refined: Call `renderReport(timeline, { story: "US-002" })` where timeline contains stories with ids "US-001", "US-002", "US-003". Assert returned string matches `/US-002/` and does not match `/US-001/|/US-003/`.

original: [renderReport] returns a string containing the text `root cause` on the failed terminal phase line when a failed story's terminal phase has `status: "fail"`.
refined: Call `renderReport(timeline)` where timeline contains a failed story with phases ending in terminal phase (name: "verify", status: "fail", isTerminal: true). Assert returned string contains "root cause" on the same line as "verify".

original: [renderReport] returns a header containing the `runId`, the `feature`, the run `status`, the story count, and the total cost.
refined: Call `renderReport(timeline)` where timeline has runId: "run-abc", feature: "my-feature", status: "failed", stories array of length 3, and cost: 0.05. Assert returned string contains "run-abc", "my-feature", "failed", "3" (or "3 stories"), and "0.05".

original: [renderReport] returns a string containing the best-effort notice indicating phases were reconstructed from logs.
refined: Call `renderReport(timeline)` where timeline has `reconstructed: true` on at least one phase. Assert returned string matches /best[- ]effort|reconstructed|from logs/i.

original: [renderReport] returns a string whose header contains `CRASHED` and that renders a placeholder for missing cost without throwing when given a `RunTimeline` with `status: "crashed"` and a story whose `cost` is `undefined`.
refined: Call `renderReport(timeline)` where timeline has status: "crashed" and a story with cost: undefined. Assert: (1) returned string contains "CRASHED", (2) no thrown error, (3) returned string contains a placeholder for missing cost (e.g., "N/A", "-", "unknown", or "0" but not undefined).

original: Given `@/replay` is imported, when the module exports are inspected, then it exposes `toReplayJson`.
refined: Import `toReplayJson` from `@/replay` and assert it is a function (typeof === 'function').

original: [toReplayJson] returns an object whose `runId`, `feature`, and `status` equal the timeline's and whose `stories` array length equals `timeline.stories.length` when given a `RunTimeline`.
refined: Call `toReplayJson(timeline)` where `timeline` is a `RunTimeline` with known `runId`, `feature`, `status`, and `stories.length = N`. Assert the returned object has `runId === timeline.runId`, `feature === timeline.feature`, `status === timeline.status`, and `stories.length === N`.

original: Given a stubbed `discoverRun`, when `runReplay("run-x", {})` is called, then `discoverRun` is invoked once with `"run-x"`.
refined: Create a spy/mock for `discoverRun`. Call `runReplay('run-x', {})`. Assert `discoverRun` was called exactly once with `'run-x'` as the first argument.

original: Given stubbed `discoverRun` and file reads that yield a known `RunTimeline`, when `runReplay(query, {})` is called, then `renderReport` is invoked once with a timeline whose `runId` matches the known value.
refined: Stub `discoverRun` to return a `RunTimeline` with `runId = 'known-run-id'`. Create a spy for `renderReport`. Call `runReplay('query', {})`. Assert `renderReport` was called exactly once and the first argument's `runId === 'known-run-id'`.

original: Given the same stubs, when `runReplay(query, { json: true })` is called, then `toReplayJson` is invoked, its serialization is written to the injected output writer, and `renderReport` is not invoked.
refined: Stub `discoverRun` to return a `RunTimeline`. Create spies for `toReplayJson` and `renderReport`. Create a mock output writer. Call `runReplay('query', { json: true })`. Assert `toReplayJson` was called exactly once, the output writer received a stringified JSON string, and `renderReport` was not called.

original: Given `@/replay` or the command module is imported, when the module exports are inspected, then it exposes `registerReplayCommand`.
refined: Import `registerReplayCommand` from `@/replay` or the commands module and assert it is a function (typeof === 'function').

original: [registerReplayCommand] adds a subcommand named `replay` that accepts an optional positional run-id and exposes a `--json` option when applied to a fresh commander `Command` instance.
refined: Create a new `Command()` instance. Call `registerReplayCommand(cmd)`. Assert `cmd.commands` contains a command with `name === 'replay'`. Call `.parse(['node', 'test', 'run-id']) on the command chain. Assert the parsed `runId` equals `'run-id'` and the command has an option matching `/--json/`.

original: Given `discoverRun` throws `NaxError { code: "RUN_NOT_FOUND" }`, when `runReplay("missing", {})` is called, then it resolves to exit code `1` and writes a message containing `"missing"` to the injected error writer.
refined: Stub `discoverRun` to throw `new NaxError({ code: 'RUN_NOT_FOUND' })`. Create a mock error writer. Call `runReplay('missing', {})`. Assert the returned exit code is `1` and the error writer received a string containing `'missing'`.

original: Given a JSONL file containing malformed lines alongside valid entries, when `runReplay(query, {})` is called, then it skips the malformed lines, writes a report from the remaining spine, and resolves to exit code `0`.
refined: Create a JSONL file with 3 entries where entry 2 is malformed (invalid JSON). Stub `discoverRun` to yield this file. Call `runReplay('query', {})`. Assert exit code is `0`, `renderReport` was called once with a timeline derived from the 2 valid entries.

original: Given an injected registry and files for a run with a crash signal and no metrics entry, when `runReplay(query, {})` is called, then it writes a report whose header contains `CRASHED` to the injected output writer and resolves to exit code `0`.
refined: Stub `discoverRun` to return a `RunTimeline` with `status: 'crashed'` and no `metrics`. Create a mock output writer. Call `runReplay('query', {})`. Assert exit code is `0` and the output writer received a string containing `'CRASHED'`.
